request: Hey Claude, I just added the "editorial-workflow-builder" skill. Our blog keeps slipping. Design our content workflow from idea to published, tell us who approves what, and how many new posts and refreshes we can really ship a month. WordPress, Search Console, GA4 and Google Sheets are connected.
business: Example Booking Software, an online booking and scheduling app for small service businesses (invented example)

inputs_from_user.current_steps: Ideas come up in a Monday chat thread. Sam picks a keyword. Leo or Ana write in Google Docs, then paste the piece into WordPress as a draft and set it to Pending. Maya edits every piece, then every piece goes to Noor in product marketing, who reviews on Fridays. Sam adds Kai's images and the meta description and publishes. Refreshes happen when someone notices an old post. Writers use an AI assistant for outlines; nobody wrote down what else it is used for.

hours_per_task.task: pick ideas from the Monday thread
upload to WordPress, meta and links

inputs_from_user.hours_note: the team's own estimates; nobody has timed them
sign_off_needed_for: named customers in a story or quote
inputs_from_user.ai_policy: No written policy. The team uses an AI assistant for outlines. Never paste customer data into it.
inputs_from_user.goal_metric: GA4 key events from blog pages
inputs_from_user.tracker: none with stage dates; work is tracked in a chat thread
inputs_from_user.status_board_spreadsheet: Content operations (spreadsheet the user named for the board)

wordpress_get_posts.note: status publish, draft, pending and future; fields id, title, status, author, date, modified, link
